statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res is the maximum of the set { hi - l | 0 <= l < hi <= len(s) and Eq(l, hi) <= 1 }, where for any 0 <= l < hi <= len(s), Eq(l, hi) is the number of indices i with l <= i < hi - 1 and s[i] = s[i+1]. In words, res is the length of a longest non-empty contiguous substring of s that has at most one adjacent pair of equal bytes.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The slice s is non-empty (1 <= n <= 50) and every byte s[i] for 0 <= i < n is an ASCII digit code, i.e. 48 <= s[i] <= 57.
